Recycling and waste management

Finding value in what is discarded

Recycling and waste management bring together environmental needs and business decisions: what can be recovered, who will use it, how it will be processed and whether the operating model is viable.

An opportunity might involve a particular waste stream, a recovery technology, an operating partnership or a market for recovered materials. Each needs its own assessment.

We see possibilities for Japanese and Indian businesses to combine technology, operating experience, local relationships and access to customers.

Questions worth exploring

  • Which waste stream or resource-recovery need should the opportunity address?
  • Is there a dependable source of material and a credible market for the recovered output?
  • Which technology and operating approach fit the local conditions?
  • How should collection, processing, quality, sales and partner responsibilities connect?

Where SetuHashi could contribute

  • Assess the business opportunity

    Examine the proposed value chain, customer demand, commercial assumptions and dependencies.

  • Find suitable partners

    Identify and assess businesses that could contribute technology, material supply, operating capabilities or access to buyers.

  • Develop workable arrangements

    Help participants define contributions, responsibilities and commercial terms, and plan a pilot or staged implementation.

A practical starting point

An assessment of one defined waste stream or recovery opportunity, including potential partners, commercial dependencies and the next decision.

Technical feasibility, environmental requirements and applicable approvals would be addressed with qualified specialists and relevant authorities.
